A REAL DEADLOCK was caught only by live device testing, not by any isolated ProviderContainer test the coder wrote: the plan's illustrative close()-then-invalidate() order hangs AppDatabase.close() forever in the real app, because AppShell's IndexedStack keeps every tab's provider subscriptions alive permanently and drift's close() (traced into drift's own source, StreamQueryStore.close()) waits for all of them to unsubscribe first - diagnosed via mcp__dart__get_runtime_errors (nothing), logcat (silent), dumpsys window (focus never left MainActivity, no share-sheet Activity was ever started), and temporary debug prints pinpointing the exact hung await; fixed by reordering to invalidate-then-close (DatabaseMaintenanceNotifier._closeCurrentDatabase()), verified live with no delay needed. A secondary related finding: because invalidating happens before the file mutation, restore()/deleteAll() can transiently race a freshly-reopened connection for the file - real and sustained on Windows (this project's dev host, holds an exclusive lock for as long as that connection stays open) but harmless on Android/iOS (the app's real targets, verified live) and on this project's own Linux CI, where POSIX tolerates deleting/overwriting an open file; a bounded retry (_retryOnFileLock) rides out genuinely transient locks without pretending to solve the Windows-only sustained case. All three operations (backup/restore/delete) verified live end-to-end on a genuinely fresh flutter run build (not hot reload/restart, to rule out stale background-isolate artifacts) - share sheet opens with the real file, restore round-trips a real picked file (pushed to the emulator's Downloads) correctly, delete resets Home/Settings to fresh-install defaults. A new regression test keeps a live financialPositionProvider listener subscribed across the call to reproduce the exact scenario none of the originally-written isolated tests could catch. a genuinely private per-file widget or plain top-level function (like FEAT05's _CategoryAutocompleteField, FEAT09/FEAT10's group_style.dart/kind_style.dart/tab_app_bar_actions.dart, FEAT11's _PersonAccountField, or FEAT15's _BudgetAllocationChart) does NOT need a diagram entry - check whether the new thing is a tracked class (Screen/Provider/DAO/Notifier) or private/shared implementation detail before halting; adding a METHOD to an already-tracked class (e.g. FEAT14's AccountDao.writeOffDebt()) still needs a diagram entry, just on the existing box, not a new one; (8) this project is a pilot run for a different target project (owner's own words, 2026-08-24) - the process trail itself is part of what gets extracted later, so keep the same discipline on these post-backlog polish items as on the original tracked issues; (9) a plain ListView(children: [...]) in a widget test does NOT build off-screen children automatically (Sliver-realized, not eager) - a widget test asserting on content below the fold must scroll first (tester.drag + pumpAndSettle), caught repeatedly across FEAT07/FEAT10's chart/card tests; (10) a subagent can hit its own session/usage limit mid-task and terminate without finishing - check `git status`/diff for partial, uncommitted work before assuming a 'failed' task notification means nothing was done; FEAT07's coder got the DAO layer fully done and correct before terminating, and that work was kept and built on rather than redone; (11) `flutter gen-l10n` is a SEPARATE required step from `dart run build_runner build` whenever an ARB file changes - build_runner alone leaves new l10n keys undefined and flutter analyze fails on undefined_getter; now documented in context/coding-conventions/dart-and-flutter.md; (12) when two issues both touch the same file (e.g. FEAT09 and FEAT10 both touch balance_sheet_screen.dart), dispatch their flutter-coder agents SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel, to avoid two agents editing the same working-tree file at once; when issues touch DISJOINT files instead (FEAT13/FEAT14/FEAT15), parallel dispatch is safe for the edits themselves but each agent's own mid-run verification commands (dart format, flutter test) can transiently observe another still-running agent's uncommitted changes in the shared tree - not a real failure, but don't trust an individual agent's report without a final merged-tree verification pass once all of them finish, and consider isolation: "worktree" if this needs to be airtight; (13) not every enum-value addition is a schema migration - a textEnum column with no CHECK constraint accepts a new legal Dart-side value with nothing more than a build_runner regen; check for a CHECK constraint before reaching for drift_dev make-migrations (FEAT11); (14) `ref.read` inside a helper does NOT subscribe the calling widget to anything - if a value needs to update as a stream emits, something in build() must `ref.watch` it too, even if the read itself happens elsewhere (FEAT11's repay-direction-toggle default stayed stuck until this was added); (15) when a visual bug report is ambiguous or hard to picture from text/a screenshot alone, connect to the owner's already-running debug build (mcp__dart__dtd to find/connect the DTD instance, adb for screenshots and uiautomator dump for exact widget bounds since guessed pixel coordinates repeatedly miss) and reproduce it live before touching code; (16) after force-stopping a running debug app to fix an unrelated issue (e.g. a bad tap coordinate), relaunching it via adb (monkey/am start) brings back the LAST INSTALLED APK, not the latest source - a hot reload only patches an already-running Dart VM, so once that process is killed, only a fresh rebuild reflects new code; this silently showed a stale screen once (FEAT12) until caught by re-verifying with a clean rebuild rather than trusting the first screenshot; (17) a user-typed or joke-named piece of DATA (an account name, a category name like FEAT14's literal 'Ikhlaskan') never goes through AppLocalizations/ARB - only chrome (button labels, screen titles) gets localized; get-or-create lookups against such data use an in-memory case-insensitive Dart compare (AccountFormScreen._nameCollides is the model), never a SQL LOWER(). (18) a Notifier's ProviderContainer unit test that only ever does c.read(someProvider) once, with no active listener, cannot catch a bug that only manifests when a real screen keeps ref.watch()-ing that provider continuously (e.g. via AppShell's IndexedStack keeping every tab mounted) - a real deadlock in AppDatabase.close() (FEAT20) went uncaught by three passing isolated tests for exactly this reason; if a fix depends on subscription/listener lifecycle timing, pin it with a test that keeps a live c.listen() subscription open across the call, and when in doubt, verify live on a real running app rather than trusting isolated-container tests alone - use a genuinely fresh flutter run (not hot reload/restart) when the bug could involve a stale background isolate, and check mcp__dart__get_runtime_errors/logcat/dumpsys window before assuming silence means nothing happened.
